requirements.requirement: /tmp mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev (program execution, setuid, device nodes ignored)
requirements.summary: findmnt output immediately after configuration (cmd-58296e6c106846b6, cmd-fe7363b963c04e76) shows /tmp as tmpfs with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec. After a full reboot, findmnt (cmd-27881145bac9456f) again shows the same options, and a functional test (cmd-3c2112a11dba4077) confirms a script placed in /tmp cannot execute (Permission denied, exit 126) post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev (program execution, setuid, device nodes ignored)
requirements.summary: findmnt output (cmd-58296e6c106846b6, cmd-fe7363b963c04e76) shows /dev/shm as tmpfs with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec immediately after remounting (previously only nosuid,nodev per cmd-07bf46a66857413f). Post-reboot findmnt (cmd-27881145bac9456f) confirms the same options persisted, and a copied binary in /dev/shm failed to execute post-reboot (cmd-3c2112a11dba4077, Permission denied, exit 126).

A full disruption/recovery cycle is directly observed: pre-reboot healthy hardened state captured (cmd-2aa7374371d6446a, boot_id 984a7d52...), reboot issued (cmd-ba21c70e95a04315), connection loss during the gap confirmed (cmd-8a80d8afbc514226, cmd-c4081dc8e516441f, cmd-669916ac09b844e8), a new boot_id observed after recovery (cmd-aa47ac21df034f95, c9102ed6...), and post-reboot findmnt (cmd-27881145bac9456f) shows both /tmp and /dev/shm still mounted with nosuid,nodev,noexec, generated from the persisted /etc/fstab entries added in cmd-8cacb794fa39496a.

overall_summary: The executor hardened /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 with nosuid,nodev,noexec via /etc/fstab, verified the live effect, then performed a genuine reboot (confirmed by differing boot_id before/after) and re-verified via findmnt and functional execution tests that the hardening persisted post-reboot. All three material outcomes are directly and coherently demonstrated across a full disruption/recovery cycle, satisfying the elevated evidentiary bar for persistence-related claims.
limitations: No independent evidence beyond the executor's own commands was available to cross-check the reboot; however the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots (before_prepare and after_executor) corroborate the same boot_id transition (984a7d52... -> c9102ed6...), increasing confidence.
A minor residual backup file (/etc/fstab.bak.<timestamp>) was left on node1; low risk but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: Mutations were minimal and purposeful: /etc/fstab was backed up before editing (cmd-cba85e17e9e54dbc, reasonable precaution) and appended with the two required tmpfs entries (cmd-8cacb794fa39496a). A `systemctl enable tmp.mount` attempt failed harmlessly because the unit is fstab-generated/transient (cmd-58296e6c106846b6) - no state change resulted. Live remounts of /tmp and /dev/shm (cmd-58296e6c106846b6) were required to apply the change immediately and are consistent with the task. Test artifacts created for functional verification (/tmp/t.sh, /dev/shm/true2 in cmd-3c2112a11dba4077) were fully removed afterward (cmd-0642272116b7443e). The one residual artifact is the /etc/fstab.bak.<timestamp> backup file (confirmed still present in cmd-0642272116b7443e), which is low-risk, non-executable, and doesn't affect functionality or security posture, but is technically unreverted executor-created residue.
